## RUN

Runner, from `03_runner.md`.

- **RUN-01** · One command with only the source root runs the whole process (P2). There are no config files (`MVP_scope.md`, section 8.1).
- **RUN-02** · Output is always the Viewer mode: JSON lines on standard output (`--human` is out of the MVP).
- **RUN-03** · A missing or unreadable source root stops the Runner with exit code 2 and a diagnostic saying what is missing or wrong. It writes nothing. The source root comes from the command line, else from the saved configuration (`RUN-29`).
- **RUN-04** · Open or create the database. Check `config_version`; if it is unknown, stop with a clear message. The first structure version is `1`; a new database is created with it. The same holds in a `--dry-run-only` pass (`RUN-23`).
- **RUN-05** · Find the tools in `app/tools/`, call each one's `--info`, and fill `config_tools`. A tool is a folder holding an executable launcher with the folder's name; any other folder is skipped, with a log line. A tool's `--info` must say whether it reads files: `readsFiles` with a required `source_root`, or `readsFiles: false` with no `source_root` and not run once per file; otherwise the Runner refuses to start (`DATA-09`). Derive the order from the `dataName`s and write `config_ordering` (`02_data_contracts.md`, DATA-11). Installation and removal are out of the MVP; the tools are simply there. The same holds in a `--dry-run-only` pass (`RUN-23`).
- **RUN-06** · List the files (`RUN-34`) and write `project_files`. The Runner does this itself (`RN-13`). The same holds in a `--dry-run-only` pass (`RUN-23`).
- **RUN-07** · For each tool in the ordering (M1 once per file), check whether its output needs refreshing, and build its JSON from the checked outputs of the earlier tools, in memory (`RUN-17` to `RUN-22`; `02_data_contracts.md`, DATA-12, DATA-13). A tool whose output is up to date is skipped; the others go on to `RUN-08`.
- **RUN-08** · Dry-run the tool with `--dry-run --stdin`, passing the JSON. Parse the last line (DATA-17):
  - **go**: continue
  - **no-go** with exit code 2: an invocation error, so a Runner bug. Log it as such and stop
  - **no-go** with exit code 1: a problem in the data. Log it as the tool's error and stop
- **RUN-09** · Run the tool for real with `--stdin` and the same JSON. Then read its `result.json` in the store it passed, the log named by `result.json`'s `logPath`, and its output.
- **RUN-10** · If the result is `failed`, stop. Otherwise write `project_outputs` and `project_tool_runs`, and go on.
- **RUN-11** · M1 is invoked once per file, dry run then real run each time. For two or three files that is a handful of processes; record the time it takes as a finding (`TS-31`). There is no timeout: a tool that hangs blocks the run until it is stopped by hand. This is a scope cut, together with cancel (`FND-34`).
- **RUN-12** · At the end, write `project_runs` and print `run_finished` with the outcome.
- **RUN-13** · `--read-cache` prints one `cache` event holding **exactly the Runner's cache** (`RUN-27`), with the records grouped by data name (`RUN-25`). It reads nothing else: not the tool stores, not the database. It starts no tool and writes nothing. With no cache yet, the event is empty.
- **RUN-14** · Every run writes `data/runner/logs/<timestamp>.log` in the shared format (DATA-16), a `--dry-run-only` pass too, with the pass marked as a dry run in its first entry (`RUN-23`).
- **RUN-15** · For every tool invocation, the log records the time, the exact command line, the JSON sent, the dry-run result and the real result. A user can repeat any step by hand from it.
- **RUN-16** · **Each tool's dry run works from the saved stores** (the MVP's answer to `RN-11`). The Runner builds a tool's JSON from what is saved: the earlier tools' outputs in their stores. Nothing passes from one dry run to the next through what it prints.
  - In a real run, each tool's dry run comes after the earlier tools' real runs, so it sees their fresh outputs.
  - In a `--dry-run-only` pass, it sees the outputs left by the last real run, so the pass previews each step against that run.
  - If the stores hold no output for a parameter, the Runner still sends the parameter, empty, so the tool's parameter check passes and the tool itself reports no-go (`TOOL-09`). As with any no-go, the Runner stops (`RUN-08`). This is the status-check warning "a missing output from an earlier tool" (`toolset.md`, section 4.3). With `ts-program` alone in the run list (`RUN-33`) it doesn't arise: every parameter of `ts-program` is one the Runner provides (`RUN-29`), none an earlier tool's output, so on a fresh data folder a `--dry-run-only` pass dry-runs `ts-program` on the listed files and reports its go, with reason `missing` (`TEST-03`).
  - The Runner takes saved outputs only for files in the current file list. If a file in the list has no saved output, or its hash differs from the one in `project_files`, the Runner sends what it has and lists those file IDs as `staleInputs` in the tool's `tool_dry_run` event. The tool's go / no-go stands.
- **RUN-17** · **Check before running.** For each invocation in the ordering (each tool, and M1 once per file), the Runner decides whether a refresh is needed (`RUN-20`). If it is, the tool is dry-run and run as in `RUN-08` to `RUN-10`. If not, the tool is skipped: the Runner prints `tool_skipped`, starts no process, and leaves the output as it is. A `--dry-run-only` pass is the exception: it is a status check, so it dry-runs every invocation, and marks those a real run would skip as `up-to-date` in their `tool_dry_run` event.
- **RUN-18** · **Shape check of the available outputs.** The Runner reads the saved outputs of every earlier tool in the ordering and checks their shape against each tool's `--info`:
  - the output file exists and parses as JSON
  - for every output the tool declares, the file holds an array under the output's `jsonKey` (`FND-01`), and the `formatVersion` recorded in the file matches the output's `formatVersion` in `--info`
  - every record has the fields `--info` maps for its kind (`represents`): an ID and a parent for nodes; a from and a to for relations (`to` may be `null`: an unresolved relation); a contained and a container field for containment; and a Location (`DATA-01`).
  - for a per-file tool, only the outputs of files in the current file list count; outputs of files no longer in the list are ignored (part of `FND-06`)

  An output that fails any of these counts as missing. The check is only of shape: it doesn't judge whether the content is right.
- **RUN-19** · **Building the inputs.** For each parameter of the next tool, the Runner finds the earlier tool whose `--info` outputs the parameter's `dataName` (`DATA-11`) and builds the value from that tool's checked outputs: **only the records of that data name**, found under the output's `jsonKey` (`DATA-18`), never the rest of the output file. From a per-file tool, one flat array: files in file ID order (`RUN-28`), each file's records in their order. From a tool run once, its records. Values with a data name no tool outputs are provided by the Runner (`RUN-29`). In a real run, the earlier tools have just been refreshed or found up to date, so their outputs are all there; if one still fails the shape check, see the errors table. In a `--dry-run-only` pass, a missing output gives an empty parameter and the tool's no-go (`RUN-16`, `TOOL-09`).
- **RUN-20** · **When a refresh is needed.** The Runner computes the invocation's **input fingerprint**: the SHA-256 of the tool's name, its `toolVersion` from `--info`, the JSON built in `RUN-19` with its keys sorted, and, for each parameter with a `files.file.*` data name, the current hash of that file from the file list. A refresh is needed, with the first matching reason, when:
  - `missing`: the tool's own saved output is absent, or fails the shape check in `RUN-18`
  - `never-run`: `project_tool_runs` has no successful run of this invocation
  - `last-failed`: its last real run failed
  - `inputs-changed`: the fingerprint differs from the one recorded for its last successful run (this covers a changed source file, a changed earlier output, and a new tool version)
  - in a `--dry-run-only` pass only, `upstream-refresh`: an earlier tool it takes input from would be refreshed. The saved outputs it would get are about to change, so it can't be judged up to date; its dry run uses the saved outputs and reports `staleInputs` (`RUN-16`)

  Otherwise the output is **up to date**. Skipping assumes tools are repeatable: the same input gives the same output (`DATA-04`, checked by `TEST-04`). For the MVP, repeatability is nice to have, not a hard requirement; the product decision depends on what the MVP finds (`MVP_scope.md`, section 1).
- **RUN-21** · **How a change spreads.** Since a tool's fingerprint covers the earlier outputs it receives, a change spreads exactly as far as outputs actually change. For a parameter that is a list of files, the fingerprint covers the current hash of every file in the list (`TSP-D11`; `buildInput` in `app/runner/src/runner.ts`). So `ts-program`, run once over the program, reruns when any listed `.ts` file changed, or a `.ts` file was added or removed; a file touched with the same content, or a file it doesn't read, leaves it skipped (`TEST-04`). A tool after it would rerun only if an output it takes changed. This is the MVP's answer to "how a change spreads" (`toolset.md`, section 5.3, to define).
- **RUN-22** · **Recording.** A real run records the fingerprint in `project_tool_runs` and `project_outputs`. A skipped invocation is recorded in `project_tool_runs` as `skipped`, with the reason `up-to-date`. When nothing changed, no tool runs and no tool output is written; the Runner still writes its log and the `project_runs` row (`RUN-12`, `RUN-14`; see `FND-37`). A `--dry-run-only` pass makes the same decisions and reports them in its `tool_dry_run` events. It records no fingerprint, no `skipped` row and no output (`RUN-23`).
- **RUN-23** · **A `--dry-run-only` pass may read anything it needs, and the Runner may write whatever is useful.** The no-write rule of a dry run binds the tools only (`toolset.md`, section 4.3).
  - It may read the database, every tool's store, the examined source and each tool's `--info`.
  - It starts like a real run: it creates the database if missing, fills `config_tools` and `config_ordering` (`RUN-04`, `RUN-05`), writes `project_files` (`RUN-06`), and writes its log (`RUN-14`) and a `project_runs` row marked as a dry run.
  - It writes nothing that records a real run: no `project_outputs` row, and no fingerprint, success or `skipped` row in `project_tool_runs`. So the next real run's refresh check (`RUN-20`) is unaffected. It may record the dry-run results in `project_tool_runs`, marked as dry runs.
  - Its report goes to standard output, as Viewer-mode events.
  - Each tool's dry run in the pass writes nothing (`TOOL-06`, `TOOL-40`).
- **RUN-24** · **The Runner checks a tool only through its input and its output:** the JSON it builds, the dry-run lines and exit code, `result.json` and the output's shape (`RUN-18`). It doesn't watch or limit what a tool reads or writes. A tool that reads more than its one file, or the database, is a design error in that tool, not a Runner error (`toolset.md`, section 4.2).
- **RUN-25** · **Matching keys to data is the Runner's job** (`DATA-18`). It finds every record only through the tools' `--info` (`jsonKey`, `fields`, parameter data names), never with tool-specific code. In the `cache` event (`RUN-13`) it hands the Viewer the records already grouped by data name, each group with the `--info` details the Viewer needs (`represents`, `containedIn`, `contains`, `fields`), so the Viewer never matches keys itself.
- **RUN-26** · **The Runner always sends `store_path`**: from the saved configuration, else the default `<zaansouvi-mvp>/data/tools/<tool>`, the layout in `01_architecture.md` (`DATA-12`, `DATA-13`, `RUN-29`). It never relies on a tool's default or on `last_run.json` for the store, and reads each tool's result and outputs only from that folder.
- **RUN-27** · **The Runner's cache** (`runner.md`, section 10.2).
  - The MVP has one implicit run configuration (`RUN-01`), so one cache: `data/runner/cache.json`.
  - **Each real run replaces it**, written to a temporary name and renamed at the end, failed runs included.
  - **What goes where.** The database keeps only what the refresh check needs: file hashes, fingerprints, the last result of each invocation, and the runs (`RUN-20`, `RUN-22`). The cache holds what the Viewer reads. The Viewer reads only the cache, through `--read-cache` (`VIEW-03`).
  - **Its shape** is one JSON object with `run`, `files`, `tools`, `invocations`, `data` and `dryRun`, described in the reference schema, section 13. Each tool output is stored once under `data`; an invocation's input points to it instead of copying it.
  - It holds the run's input, result and intermediate data: run ID, outcome and times; the file list; the record of tools and the order used; for each invocation, the JSON sent, the dry-run result, the tool's `result.json`, and `skipped` with its reason; and the data each tool produced, grouped by data name with its `--info` details. Outputs of tools skipped as up to date are read from their stores (`RUN-18`) and included, so the cache always describes the whole current state.
  - It holds only tools in the current record and files in the current file list, so after check C1 or a deleted file the old data is gone from what the Viewer sees (`FND-06`).
  - Per-file results come from the cache too: M1 keeps one `result.json` per store, but the cache keeps each invocation's result.
  - **A `--dry-run-only` pass leaves alone the part of the cache the Viewer draws from** (`runner.md`, section 10.2). It replaces only a separate dry-run part: for each invocation, `go` or `no-go`, the refresh reason or `up-to-date`, the error, the diagnostics from the tool's go line (`DATA-17`) and `staleInputs`. After a real run, each invocation's diagnostics are in its `result` in the cache. The Viewer may show that part, but never in the graph. A real run replaces the whole cache, dry-run part included, which drops it.
  - Tools never read it; they work only from their inputs and manage their own cache if they need one.
- **RUN-28** · **One fixed order: sorted by file ID.** The Runner handles files in order of their file ID, by plain string comparison (character codes, case-sensitive: JavaScript's default sort). A per-file tool is invoked in that order, and every array the Runner builds by file follows it: the file list, a `list` parameter of file IDs (`ts-program`'s `files`), the records it gathers from per-file outputs, and the Runner's cache. The order affects no tool output: `ts-program` gets the files as one list, sorts them itself, and its output doesn't depend on their order (`TPG-25`). It makes the stop point after a failure, the events, the fingerprint (`RUN-20`) and the cache the same on every run. For `test-source-mvp2`, the `files` given to `ts-program`: `src/app.ts`, `src/report/charts/bars.ts`, `src/report/format.ts`, `src/report/summary.ts`, `src/shapes.ts`, `src/util/numbers.ts`.
- **RUN-29** · **Data the Runner provides** (`runner.md`, section 4). The Runner provides every value tools require that no tool produces. It reads the value from the saved configuration (the `config_` tables); if it isn't there, it creates it from a default; if the value isn't valid, it fails before any tool starts.
  - `files.file.id`, `files.file.path`: from the file list it builds (`RUN-06`, `RUN-28`). The order of the tools is derived the same way, from `--info` (`RUN-05`).
  - `zaansouvi.store_path`: default `<zaansouvi-mvp>/data/tools/<tool>` (`RUN-26`).
  - `project.source_root`: **user-defined, with no default.** It comes from the command line; the Runner saves it in `config_settings` and reads it back when a run gives none, for example from the Viewer's run button. If it is missing, the Runner prints a diagnostic saying what is missing and how to give it, and exits 2 (`RUN-03`). This is internal to the Runner and the Viewer; it goes only to tools that read files, those that declare `source_root` (`DATA-09`), and every file path they receive depends on it.
  - A required parameter whose data name is neither output by a tool nor in this list stops the Runner before any tool starts, with a diagnostic naming the tool and the parameter, exit 2. An optional parameter that doesn't affect the output is not sent (`TOOL-43`).
- **RUN-30** · **One run at a time** (`runner.md`, section 4).
  - When a run starts, the Runner creates `data/runner/run.lock` with an exclusive create, holding its process ID and start time. It removes the lock when the run ends, whatever the outcome.
  - If the lock already exists and its process is alive, the new run prints a diagnostic naming the running run and exits 2, writing nothing. If its process is gone, the lock is stale: the Runner takes it over and notes it in its log.
  - A `--dry-run-only` pass takes the lock too; `--read-cache` doesn't (the cache is replaced in one step, `RUN-27`).
  - Tools take no lock; they are assumed to run only from the Runner. A tool run by hand is the user's action. If it changed an output, the problem shows up only when that output is read as wrong input: the Runner's shape check (`RUN-18`) or the reading tool's own checks (`E12`) detect it and write an error and a diagnostic.
- **RUN-31** · **The Runner's exit codes**: `0` when the run finished, including when every invocation was skipped; `1` when a tool's no-go or failure stopped it; `2` for an invocation or start-up error: a bad or missing source root, missing user data, the lock held by another run, an unknown database version, a provided value that isn't valid, or a required parameter nobody provides. `run_finished` carries the exit code.
- **RUN-32** · **The Runner starts every tool in its data folder** (`<zaansouvi-mvp>/data`), never in the folder it was itself started from, so a Runner started from inside the examined source never runs a tool there (`E14`; `runner.md`, section 4). Checked: a run started from `test-source/src` succeeds and writes nothing into the source.
- **RUN-33** · **[Decided]** **A hardcoded list of the tools to run** (`42_tool_ts_program.md`, `TPG-D1`). The Runner holds, in its code, the names of the tools it runs, and checks the list against the folders in `app/tools/` (`RUN-05`): a listed tool with no folder or no executable launcher stops the run before any tool starts, saying which; a tool folder not in the list is not run, and the Runner reports it as not listed. M1 (`file-symbols`) is not in the list (`TPG-01`). **The list holds `ts-program` alone** (`TPG-06`): M2 and M3 are not run either, to see whether TypeScript's data alone gives a correct graph in the Viewer. This narrows `RUN-05`; the order still comes from `--info` alone. *(Naming tools in the Runner's code is a deliberate exception to "no code for any tool" (`RUN-25`, `FND-43`) for MVP 2; the product's way to add or omit tools is the named configurations of `runner.md`, section 2.)*
- **RUN-34** · **[Decided]** **The Runner lists every file, accurately.** The file list is every file under the source root, not only the files some tool reads; each tool still gets only the files its patterns match (`readsFile`, `DATA-23`). **[Proposed]** what "accurately" means:
  - **every regular file**, hidden files (names starting with `.`) included, at any depth;
  - **nothing dropped silently:** a folder skipped as a whole (**decided**, `RUN-34b`: `node_modules` and `.git`) is reported with how many files it holds and its size, and shown as a folder node (`UI-48`); a symbolic link is listed as a link, not followed (`SEC-2`); an entry that is neither a file nor a folder, or can't be read, is listed with the reason;
  - **path and size for every file; a content hash only for files some tool reads,** which change detection needs (`RUN-17` to `RUN-22`), so no other file is opened;
  - sorted by file ID (`RUN-28`); `files_listed` gives the total, the skipped folders, and each tool's count of matching files;
  - *(As built, `FND-98`: `listEntries` in `app/runner/src/runner.ts`; statuses by access checks for the user who ran the Runner; links listed with their target and whether they lead outside, never followed; `files_listed` with `folderCount`, `skippedFolders`, `perTool`, `ignoreFiles`. A tool given its files as a list with none to read stops the run before it starts, with a message built from its `--info` (the generic answer to `FND-75`). `RUN-33`'s list is `RUN_LIST` in `app/runner/src/tools.ts`; tool folders not listed give `tool_not_listed` events and the cache's `notListed`.)*
  - **[Decided]** (`RUN-34a`): **ignore files are not applied**; every file is listed, and each run says ignore files were not applied. Marking ignored files may come later as a status (`UI-48`). *(This differs from `toolset.md`, section 6.2, [Proposed], which has the Runner apply them; that item is the product's and stays as it is.)*
- **RUN-34a** (defined in `97_second_implementation.md`) · **Decides:** Ignore files · **Decision:** not applied; every file listed; each run says ignore files were not applied · **Where:** `03_runner.md`
- **RUN-34b** (defined in `97_second_implementation.md`) · **Decides:** Folders skipped as a whole · **Decision:** `node_modules` and `.git`, shown as folder nodes with file count and size · **Where:** `03_runner.md`
- **RUN-35** · **[Decided]** **The listing records each entry's status, and lists folders** (`UI-48`). While listing (`RUN-34`), from the file system alone, opening no file:
  - **for every file:** hidden (its name starts with `.`), a symbolic link (its target, and whether it lands inside or outside the source), read-only, unreadable (with the reason); also executable, empty and size, shown in words only;
  - **read-only and unreadable are judged for the user who ran the Runner** (by access checks, not mode bits);
  - **every folder is listed too, `node_modules` and `.git` included,** each with the number of files it holds, and its total size where available; the folders skipped as a whole (`RUN-34`) are counted, not listed file by file;
  - stored with each entry in the cache's file list, where the Viewer reads them (`UI-48`); `project_files` holds only each file's ID, size and content hash (`02_data_contracts.md`, tables). Whether `project_files` should hold the statuses too is `M2Q-17`.

## TEST

Test plan, from `06_test_plan.md`.

- **TEST-01** · Starting from an empty data folder (delete `data/`), the Runner runs on the copy of `test-source-mvp2`: the run succeeds with exit code 0; `ts-program` runs once, with refresh reason `missing`; and its output matches `expected-mvp2/` exactly (`tests/ts-program/check.mjs` on the tool's output folder).
- **TEST-02** · Run after TEST-01, so the store holds a real run's outputs (`RUN-16`). A `--dry-run-only` pass exits 0 and reports `go` for `ts-program`, marked `up-to-date` and with no `staleInputs`, and leaves the tools' stores (`data/tools/`) unchanged (compare file hashes before and after).
- **TEST-03** · With `data/tools/` deleted, a `--dry-run-only` pass exits 0 and reports `go` for `ts-program`, with reason `missing`; no tool writes any output.
- **TEST-04** · Refresh check (`RUN-17` to `RUN-22`, `TSP-D11`), each step after a real run:
  - **Nothing changed:** a second run skips `ts-program` (`tool_skipped`) and starts no tool.
  - **A file touched, its content the same** (a new modification time on `src/app.ts`): still skipped.
  - **A file changed** (a line appended to `src/app.ts`): `ts-program` runs, with reason `inputs-changed`, and succeeds.
  - **A `.ts` file added** (`src/extra.ts`): `ts-program` runs, given 7 files.
  - **Its outputs deleted:** `ts-program` runs, with reason `missing`.
  - **A file no tool reads added** (`notes.txt`): still skipped.
- **TEST-05** · After a real run, `zaansouvi-run --read-cache`: one `cache` event; `run.outcome` is `succeeded`; `files` lists every entry, folders included, in ID order (`README.md`, `src`, `src/app.ts`, `src/report`, `src/report/charts`, `src/report/charts/bars.ts`, `src/report/format.ts`, `src/report/summary.ts`, `src/shapes.ts`, `src/util`, `src/util/numbers.ts`); `tools` lists `ts-program` alone, and the three other tool folders are reported as not listed; `data` holds 120 `code.symbol`, 182 `code.reference` and 20 `code.link` records.
- **TEST-06** · M3 against `expected/symbol-scope.json`; **TEST-07** M3 on nested functions and file-level symbols; **TEST-08** M1 to M3 run by hand, byte-identical.
- **TEST-07** · M3 on nested functions and file-level symbols (listed with `TEST-06`)
- **TEST-08** · M1 to M3 run by hand, byte-identical (listed with `TEST-06`)
- **TEST-09** · `tests/viewer/check-model.mjs`: the graph model built from `expected/runner-cache.json` matches `expected/graph-views.json` view by view (nodes, stubs, the "this" node, edges with their counts and kinds, unresolved counts); two builds give the same bytes; six damaged caches give the expected invalid or extra items (`BE-91`, `BE-92`).
- **TEST-10** · `tests/viewer/check-server.mjs`: the backend on a temporary copy of the MVP, whose data it makes itself by running the copied Runner on a copy of `test-source-mvp2` (`ts-program` alone, `RUN-33`): the token, `Host` and `Origin` checks, the 64 KiB limit, sources, the graph (format 2, 32 views, nothing invalid or extra; the top view's 1 unresolved use and 25 built-ins; every listed entry a node) and its storing, reads limited to listed files a tool read and to `data/` (a range with `end`, a listed file no tool read, a symbolic link out included), the activity log (deleted while running, unknown events, Clear), a run and a refused second run, and bad data across restarts (partly invalid, failed, an entry in another format, a damaged `sources.json`, cleared Runner data). 37 checks (`BE-92` to `BE-94`). The 32-check version on MVP 1's data is `tests/viewer/check-server-stage1.mjs`.

## TOOL

Tools, from `04_tools.md`.

- **TOOL-01** · Options: `--info`, `--dry-run`, `--json <path>`, `--stdin`, `--log <path>`.
- **TOOL-02** · Parameters are read in the decided order (`toolset.md`, section 4.5): command-line arguments, then `--json` or `--stdin` (both together is an invocation error), then `last_run.json`. With none of these, the tool fails with an invocation error and writes nothing.
- **TOOL-03** · Parameter check: only **shape** problems are invocation errors (exit 2, nothing written): a required parameter missing, a value of the wrong type, JSON that doesn't parse. **Value** problems are run errors (exit 1, logged).
- **TOOL-04** · Once the parameters pass the check, the tool writes `last_run.json`, then does its work, writing its log as it goes.
- **TOOL-05** · On success it writes its output and `result.json` with `succeeded`. On a run error it writes `result.json` with `failed` and the error, writes no output, and leaves the earlier output as it was. Output is written to a temporary name and renamed at the end, so it is never half-written.
- **TOOL-06** · A dry run does the same work and prints its findings and a final `go` / `no-go` line to standard output (DATA-17). It reads what a real run reads (`TOOL-40`), but writes nothing at all: no output, no result, no log, no `last_run.json`, no internal state and no temporary file (`toolset.md`, section 4.3).
- **TOOL-07** · `--log <path>` also copies the log to that file. The log in the tool's data folder is always written.
- **TOOL-08** · Extra values in the JSON are ignored.
- **TOOL-09** · **A dry run works only from the input it is given, and says no-go when there is none.** It reads its input exactly as a real run would: M1 reads the source file; M2 and M3 read the earlier outputs in their JSON, which the Runner takes from the saved stores (`RUN-16`). A required input that is present but empty, for example `symbols: []`, is a run error: no-go with `E12` ("lacks what the tool needs"), exit 1, and a message naming the missing data name, for example `code.symbol`. The tool never previews from nothing. A missing source file is `E6`, as in a real run. The same rule holds in a real run, which fails with the same error. `ts-program` takes no other tool's output: its dry run reads the files it is given in `files`, as a real run does (`TPG-23`). It checks that `source_root` is a folder and that every listed file lies inside it, is a `.ts` file and exists, then builds the program and checks every file's syntax, with no checker; any of these failing is `E12` (a missing listed file included), no-go, exit 1. A source with no file for it to read is stopped by the Runner before `ts-program` starts (`RUN-34`).
- **TOOL-10** · parse with the parser, no type checking (listed under M1 `file-symbols`)
- **TOOL-11** · the symbols it lists (listed under M1 `file-symbols`)
- **TOOL-12** · references, not property names after a dot (listed under M1 `file-symbols`)
- **TOOL-13** · resolve references within the same file (listed under M1 `file-symbols`)
- **TOOL-14** · reference kinds: declaration, write, call, read (listed under M1 `file-symbols`)
- **TOOL-20** · link imports from the symbol records alone (listed under M2 `cross-file-links`)
- **TOOL-21** · package specifiers give `external` (listed under M2 `cross-file-links`)
- **TOOL-22** · M2 checks only its own input (listed under M2 `cross-file-links`)
- **TOOL-23** · use-site links for imported names (listed under M2 `cross-file-links`)
- **TOOL-24** · M2's remaining rules and invocation errors (listed under M2 `cross-file-links`)
- **TOOL-30** · a file scope and top-level function scopes (listed under M3 `symbol-scope`)
- **TOOL-31** · assigning symbols to scopes (listed under M3 `symbol-scope`)
- **TOOL-32** · a function without a `range` fails (listed under M3 `symbol-scope`)
- **TOOL-33** · each scope names its owner (listed under M3 `symbol-scope`)
- **TOOL-34** · where scopes are placed (listed under M3 `symbol-scope`)
- **TOOL-35** · the order of scopes and memberships (listed under M3 `symbol-scope`)
- **TOOL-36** · M3's run and invocation errors (listed under M3 `symbol-scope`)
- **TOOL-40** · **What a tool reads:** its JSON, its `last_run.json`, its own store and internal state, and, for M1, the one file it is given. A tool that needs more than one file, or the database, is a design error in that tool (`toolset.md`, section 4.2). It writes only to its own store, and nothing in a dry run (`TOOL-06`). None of this is checked by the Runner (`RUN-24`). **The exception is a program tool** (`TSP-D3`; `toolset.md`, section 4.2, `TS-37`), which states `"scope": "program"` in its `readsFiles`: `ts-program` reads, in one invocation, every listed `.ts` file it is given in `files`, and TypeScript's own library, nothing else from the source (its compiler host shows TypeScript only those files, `TPG-20`; checked by its read log, `TOOL-52`).
- **TOOL-41** · **Each tool is responsible for producing correct output** (`toolset.md`, section 4.2). It checks its parameters, and its result where it needs to, and fails with a run error rather than write something wrong. The Runner's refresh check (`RUN-17` to `RUN-22`) decides whether to run a tool; it doesn't make the tool's output correct.
- **TOOL-42** · **Agreed key names** (`DATA-19`). Every key a tool writes, in its output, `--info`, `result.json`, `last_run.json` and dry-run lines, has the one meaning agreed for that name, as listed in the reference schema (`DATA-20`). A tool that needs a new meaning uses a new name. It reads the records in its input by those agreed names; it doesn't read another tool's `--info` (`DATA-18`).
- **TOOL-43** · **Parameters that affect the output, and those that don't** (`toolset.md`, section 4.5).
  - Each parameter in `--info` carries `affectsOutput`. Those with `true` follow `TOOL-02` exactly.
  - Those with `false`, such as `store_path` (`DATA-21`), are optional. If one is missing, the tool uses its default, or works it out from the input by its own means, without affecting the Runner; if it can do neither, it fails early. For `store_path`, the default is `./zaansouvi/tools/<tool>/` in the working folder.
  - `last_run.json` is only ever a complete input (`TOOL-02`), never a source for one missing parameter.
  - The tool records, for each one, whether the input gave it or its default applied (`nonOutputParameterSources`: `input` or `default`) in its log and `result.json`.
  - The output never depends on these parameters.
- **TOOL-44** · A tool returns its diagnostics with its work, and the tool helper writes them into `result.json` and onto the dry run's go line (`DATA-14`, `DATA-17`); they never go in an output file or `--info`. M1 does this from version 0.5.0.
- **TOOL-45** · **M1, M2, M3 and `ts-program` implement `TOOL-01` to `TOOL-08`, `TOOL-43` and `DATA-14` to `DATA-17` through the tool helper** in `app/tool-helper/` (`ARCH-02`, `TPG-10`). The helper knows nothing about any specific tool; each tool supplies only its `--info`, its parameter checks and its work.
- **TOOL-50** · `ts-program` 0.2.0 (`app/tools/ts-program/`): runs TypeScript's own compiler over every listed `.ts` file in one invocation (a program tool, `toolset.md`, section 4.2, `TS-37`), and writes per source file its declarations, every use resolved to the declaration TypeScript names, and its import links. Design: `42_tool_ts_program.md`; what a correct output is: `41_typescript_program_plan.md`, section 1.1; records: the MVP 2 schema (`DATA-24`), with 0.2.0's `declaredWith`, `defaultExport` and the `override` and `accessor` modifiers (`FND-110`).
- **TOOL-51** · Parameters: `source_root`, `files` (a list), `configs` (refused in 0.2.0, `TPG-D4a`), `store_path`. With no configuration, the options of `tsc --init`. Syntax errors stop it (`E12`); type errors are counted, never a stop. Its dry run checks the parameters and the syntax, with no checker.
- **TOOL-52** · Checks: `tests/ts-program/check.mjs` (exact match with `expected-mvp2/`), `tests/ts-program/check-definitions.mjs` (every edge against TypeScript's "go to definition", `FND-99`), determinism, and the read log (only the listed files and TypeScript's library).

## TPG

The ts-program tool, from `42_tool_ts_program.md`.

- **TPG-01** · **[Decided]** **M1 (`file-symbols`) remains as it is,** code, tests and expected results unchanged, and is **explicitly not run by the Runner for now**. It can still be run by hand, and serves as the first stage's record and a point of comparison (section 10).
- **TPG-02** · **[Decided]** **A new tool, `ts-program`, whose purpose is explicitly running TypeScript** to extract the data the graph needs, and to process it in a way useful for further processing.
- **TPG-03** · **[Decided]** **It keeps in line with the existing contracts, but new keys are allowed in its JSON input and output:** the same options, JSON parameters, `--info`, data names, record shapes, `result.json`, logs, store and dry run as every tool (`04_tools.md`, `TOOL-01` to `TOOL-09`; `02_data_contracts.md`), extended where a correct graph needs more.
- **TPG-04** · **[Decided]** **The Runner runs a hardcoded list of tools, checked against the folders that exist** (`TPG-D1`; `03_runner.md`, `RUN-33`). M1 is not in it.
- **TPG-05** · **[Decided]** **`ts-program` runs TypeScript inside its own invocation and transforms what it can into the Viewer's format** (`TPG-D2`): its outputs are records the Viewer reads directly (`represents`, `fields` roles, `containedIn`), as far as the compiler's data allows.
- **TPG-06** · **TPG-06 Closed** **`ts-program`'s output is enough:** the Viewer builds a correct graph from `ts-program`'s records alone, with no further tool between them (links in M2's role, scopes in M3's, or others). **MVP 2 runs `ts-program` alone** (`RUN-33`), and the graph TypeScript's data gives in the Viewer is judged against the definition of a correct graph (`41_typescript_program_plan.md`, section 1.1) and the expected graph of `test-source-mvp2`. The one gap, frames, is closed by drawing a frame for any entered container (`TSP-D8`, `UI-37`; `FND-99`). Where the graph falls short, the shortfall is recorded, and only then is a tool (links, scopes, other) or a change to `ts-program` or the Viewer considered.
- **TPG-10** · **[Decided]** Name **`ts-program`**, in `app/tools/ts-program/`, on the tool helper (`TOOL-45`), like M2 and M3. Its dependency is the `typescript` package (pinned, as M1's), used as the compiler: parser, binder and type checker.
- **TPG-11** · **[Decided]** **One job:** build TypeScript's program from the examined source, ask its checker what every declaration and every use is, and write that as records. It does no graph work (no levels, no lifting), no scope grouping beyond what TypeScript states (declarations inside declarations), and no presentation.
- **TPG-12** · **[Decided]** **Invocation: once per run, over the whole program** (`invocation: "once"`), writing **one output file per source file**, so the per-file shape of the data the other programs read stays as it is. This uses the exception for program tools discussed in section 8 (`toolset.md`, section 4.2, `TS-37`).
- **TPG-13** · **[Decided]** Unknown keys are ignored, as for every tool (`TOOL-08`).
- **TPG-20** · **[Decided]** **Build the program** from `files` and the compiler options (section 3.1), through a compiler host that shows TypeScript **only those files and its own library** (the strict host of `FND-83`): no probing of other paths, no `node_modules`, no `@types`. Imports of packages stay unresolved, each with a reason.
- **TPG-21** · **[Decided]** **Syntax errors** in any file make the run fail (`E12`, naming each file and position): a file TypeScript can't parse gives a wrong graph. **Type errors are not the tool's concern**: they don't stop the run; their count goes in `result.json`, and a name TypeScript can't resolve is an unresolved reference, as below.
  - On `test-source-mvp2`, `result.json` counts 2 type errors: the missing `./extra` and the decorator's signature.
- **TPG-22** · **[Decided]** **Walk every file's declarations and uses** and resolve each through the checker (`getSymbolAtLocation`), following import aliases to the declaration they name (section 5).
- **TPG-23** · **[Decided]** **Its dry run** checks the parameters, that every file exists inside `source_root` and parses; it builds the program through the same host and checks syntax only, with no checker. Go or no-go as every tool (`TOOL-06`, `TOOL-09`).
- **TPG-24** · **[Decided]** **Its log** lists every file the compiler opened, by kind (source file, library), so a check can prove it read nothing else (`TSP-04`).
- **TPG-25** · **[Decided]** **Deterministic:** the same files and options give byte-identical outputs, whatever the order of `files` (`FND-58`): records sorted by ID, keys in a fixed order, no times in outputs.
- **TPG-30** · **[Decided]** One link per import symbol, from the import to the declaration it names, **in M2's shape** (`DATA-06`: `id`, `from`, `to`, `kind: "import"`, `moduleSpecifier`, `importedName`, `reason` when unresolved), resolved by TypeScript instead of by name: default and namespace imports and re-exports included. `ts-program` produces these links itself (`TPG-D2`).
- **TPG-31** · **[Decided]** No scopes: grouping into scopes stays M3's, from `parent` (section 7). No diagnostics in outputs: they go in `result.json` (`DATA-14`). No types of expressions, beyond what resolution needs.
- **TPG-40** · **[Decided]** Exact match with expected results written by hand first, on the test source of MVP 2 (`97_second_implementation.md`, section 3.3), across files.
- **TPG-41** · **[Decided]** The read log shows only the listed files and TypeScript's library (`TSP-04`).
- **TPG-42** · **[Decided]** Determinism: two runs, and a run with `files` reversed, give byte-identical outputs.
- **TPG-43** · **[Proposed]** Broken inputs: a syntax error in one file (no-go, naming it); a file outside `source_root`; an empty `files`; a malformed configuration (no-go), an `extends` to a package (reported), several configurations (only the root one used, the others reported).
- **TPG-50** · **[Proposed]** M1's tests keep passing as they are. A comparison check runs M1 by hand and `ts-program` on the first stage's test source and lists every difference in symbols and references: evidence of what the first stage got wrong, for the findings note.
- **TPG-D1** · **Question:** **How M1 is omitted** · **Decision:** **[Decided]** a hardcoded list of tools to run in the Runner, checked against the folders; M1 is not in it (`TPG-04`, `RUN-33`)
- **TPG-D2** · **Question:** **Links: `ts-program` or M2** · **Decision:** **[Decided]** links come from `ts-program`, not M2: `ts-program` runs TypeScript in its invocation and transforms what it can into the Viewer's format, links included (`TPG-05`). No further processing after it is needed (`TPG-06`)
- **TPG-D3** · **Question:** **Types in the graph** · **Decision:** **[Decided]** by the definition of a correct graph (`41_typescript_program_plan.md`, section 1.1): interfaces and type aliases are symbols; uses in type positions are references of kind `type`, which the Viewer can hide
- **TPG-D4** · **Question:** **Where compiler options come from** (`TSP-D5`) · **Decision:** **[Decided]** section 3.1: `ts-config` reads each config as written; `ts-program` merges them with TypeScript's API. The configuration that applies is the root `tsconfig.json`; an `extends` to a package is reported; a malformed config is a no-go
- **TPG-D4a** (defined in `97_second_implementation.md`) · **Decides:** `ts-config` in the run list · **Decision:** not yet: `ts-program` runs on TypeScript's defaults, noted in each run's result · **Where:** `42`, 3.1
- **TPG-D5** · **Question:** **Built-ins** · **Decision:** **[Decided]** `to: null`, `reason: "built-in"`, `builtin` the name (section 5.2); listed apart in Problems, not counted as unresolved; built-in nodes later if wanted
- **TPG-D6** · **Question:** **IDs of merged declarations** · **Decision:** **[Decided]** the first declaration's position in source order (the three signatures of `total`: line 44; the `label` pair: the getter's); the others listed in `declarations`. Stability of IDs across edits stays a separate question
- **TPG-D7** · **Question:** **`from` and `enclosing` duplicates** (`FND-60`, item 6) · **Decision:** **[Decided]** **`ts-program` writes `from` and `to` only**, no `enclosing` or `symbol`: two names for one meaning breaks `DATA-19`; the Viewer finds them through `fromField` and `toField`
- **TPG-D8** (defined in `97_second_implementation.md`) · **Package type declarations in the program:** open, asked as `M2Q-10`.

- **TSP-D1** · **Question:** **Inside the MVP, or after it** · **Decision:** **[Decided]** **a second stage of the MVP, MVP 2**, its main goal a correct graph from real TypeScript data, correctness before consistency (`MVP_scope.md`, section 1.2) · **Changes:** `MVP_scope.md` section 1.2; sections 3 to 8 to be rewritten for MVP 2
- **TSP-D2** · **Question:** **How M1 runs** · **Decision:** **[Decided]** `ts-program`, not M1, runs once over the whole program (`invocation: "once"`) and writes one output file per source file (`42_tool_ts_program.md`, `TPG-12`) · **Changes:** `toolset.md` 4.2; `runner.md`; `DATA-08`; the Runner and the tool helper
- **TSP-D3** · **Question:** **The exception to "a tool reads one file per invocation"** · **Decision:** **[Decided]** a named class, **program tools** (`toolset.md`, section 4.2, `TS-37`): a tool may read every listed file of its one file type in one invocation when its language can only be understood as a whole program. ## UI

Viewer page, from `50_viewer_ui.md`.

- **UI-01** · **[Known]** the backend is started by hand from a shell, `zaansouvi-view [--port <n>]`, and prints the URL to open, with its token, on standard output; it doesn't open the browser itself, and runs until stopped by hand (`VIEW-07`).
- **UI-02** · **[Suggested]** the printed message, one line per fact, plain text:

    ```
    ZaAnSouVi Viewer 0.1.0
    Open in your browser: http://127.0.0.1:4310/?token=<token>
    Stop with Ctrl + C.
    ```

    A port already in use prints `Port 4310 is in use. Start with --port <n> to use another.` and exits (`VIEW-07`).
- **UI-03** · **[Suggested]** opening the page without the token, or with a wrong one, shows only a short text: "This page needs the link printed by zaansouvi-view." Nothing else is served (`FND-60`, item 3).
- **UI-10** · **[Known]** the page has a **header** linking to the pages, a **graph area**, a **details drawer** and a **status bar**, and shows where the user is in the levels, for example as a breadcrumb (`viewer.md`, sections 4.8 and 4.10).
- **UI-11** · **[Suggested]** The arrangement, for a desktop browser window:

    ```
    +----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
    | ZaAnSouVi  [Viewer]  Config  Status  Runs  | Source: [test-source v] [Run] [Dry run] |
    +----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
    | test-source > main.ts > run                                 | Details|Tools|Problems|Legend |
    | +----------------------------------------------------------+ |                     |
    | |                                                          | |  (drawer, about     |
    | |                       graph area                         | |   360 px wide)      |
    | |                                                          | |                     |
    | +----------------------------------------------------------+ |                     |
    +----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
    ```

    The line above the status bar is the activity line (`UI-65`), collapsed to the latest entry; `[^]` expands it; the count "shown / logged" stands at the start of its controls (`UI-73`).

- **UI-14** · **[Suggested]** a light and a dark theme following the system setting; nothing to configure.

Exception: a layout whose buttons are better placed otherwise for their function, such as run configurations. Followed by the zoom controls (`UI-46`), the This view / All toggle in Problems (`UI-57`) and the activity line (`UI-73`).
- **UI-20** · **[Known]** the user picks the examined source: the page lists the sources the Viewer has cached and takes a new source root; picking one shows its cached graph at once, marked with its run's time (`VIEW-08`).

The Runner sends no event for such a tool (`tool_skipped` means up to date only), so the page works this out from the tool list, generically. A dry run stops at its first no-go the same way (`invoke` in `app/runner/src/runner.ts`, both modes). During a run, `waiting` becomes `not run` when the run ends failed.

- **UI-62** · **[Decided]** **Every entry has a level: `minimal`, `normal` or `verbose`** (`VIEW-17`). The backend tags each entry when it logs it. Suggested assignment, each entry still marked "you" or "app" (not only by color, `UI-40`):
  - **`minimal`**, what a session must show: the Viewer started (its version); a run or dry run finished, with its outcome and its number of errors; a run's output partly invalid, or unusable (`VIEW-16`); a cached entry that couldn't be used (`VIEW-08`); a request refused because a run is in progress (`VIEW-05`); any error of the backend itself.
  - **`normal`**, the ordinary course of a session: you opened, added or switched a source (with its path); you started a run or a dry run; a run or dry run started, on its source root; the checks of a run's output (nothing invalid, or the counts of invalid records and extra data, `VIEW-15`); a cached graph loaded for a source (with its run's time); you switched between the latest run and the last good graph (`UI-70`); you opened a log.
  - **`verbose`**, for debugging: you entered or left a level, and which node; you selected a node or edge; each Runner event as it arrives (`tool_skipped`, `tool_dry_run`, `tool_run`, with tool, file and reason); each request the page made to the backend and its answer (endpoint, status, time taken); each invalid record and each piece of extra data, one entry per item; the graph built (node and edge counts per level).
  - **Not logged at all:** zooming and dragging, which happen continuously.
  - Each level includes only its own entries; showing several levels interleaves them in time order.
- **UI-63** · **[Decided]** **The activity line has a toggle to show or hide each level**. **[Suggested]** three small toggle buttons at the line's right end, **Minimal**, **Normal** and **Verbose**, each on or off, next to the expand button; by default Minimal and Normal are on and Verbose is off. The collapsed line shows the latest entry among the levels shown; the expand button counts the entries shown. Each entry shows its level as a short tag (`min`, `norm`, `verb`) before its text. The toggles change only what is shown, never what is logged; the choice is remembered by the page for that browser (a convenience, not Viewer data).
- **UI-64** · Not in force: the activity log is one file, appended to, as `UI-71` gives it. Its text: `mvp1/docs_2026-11-10/50_viewer_ui.md`.
- **UI-65** · **[Decided]** **An activity line at the bottom of the page lists every command and action the user or the app has carried out in the session** (`FND-66`). **MVP only, for debugging and tracking** what happened during a session; it is not part of the product's page (`viewer.md`, section 4.8). Collapsed, it is one line showing only the latest entry; expanded, it floats over the page and scrolls through everything done since the session began. Examples given by the user: *user opened folder "x" for examination*; *dry run resulted in 0 errors*; *user executed manual run*.
- **UI-66** · **[Suggested]** Placement and behavior:
  - one full-width line directly above the status bar (`UI-11`), always visible, with the entry's time (local, `HH:MM:SS`) and its text; a button at its right end, labeled with the number of entries, expands it;
  - expanded, it opens upward as a floating panel over the graph and the drawer, without moving them, about a third of the window high, newest entry at the bottom, scrolled to the end; it scrolls back to the session's first entry. Clicking the button again, pressing Escape, or clicking outside collapses it;
  - a new entry while it is collapsed replaces the line; while expanded, it is appended, and the panel stays where the user scrolled unless it was at the end;
  - entries are plain text, never HTML (`VIEW-40`), and can be selected and copied.
- **UI-67** · Not in force: entries are as `UI-62` gives them (by level, including navigation and selection at the verbose level). Its text: `mvp1/docs_2026-11-10/50_viewer_ui.md`.
- **UI-68** · **[Suggested]** an entry with more detail behind it (a run's result, the problems found) can be clicked to open that detail in the drawer (**Tools** or **Problems**). The activity line is a summary for people; the full record of a run stays in the Runner's and the tools' logs.
- **UI-69** · **[Suggested]** **the session** is the backend's: from `zaansouvi-view` starting until it stops. (The file, `UI-71`, keeps every session until it is cleared; the activity line shows the current session, from memory.) The backend keeps the entries in memory and sends them to the page, so reloading the page, or opening a second tab, shows the whole session. They are not saved: a new backend starts an empty session, beginning with "Viewer started". (Saving them in the Viewer's store, `VIEW-06`, could come later.) Runs started outside the Viewer, from the command line, don't appear, since the Viewer doesn't see them happen; a later load of their result does.
- **UI-70** · **[Known]** a view never mixes data from two runs (`viewer.md`, section 6); the banners switch the whole view between the two.
- **UI-71** · **[Decided]** **The backend writes the activity log to a single file, appending to it if it exists** (`VIEW-17`): `data/viewer/activity.log`. Every entry, every level, goes in; the level toggles (`UI-63`) never change what is written. **The format is the shared log format** (`DATA-16`; `DATA-19`): one entry per line, `<ISO time> TAB <level> TAB <event> TAB <JSON details>`, where `level` is the severity (`info`, `warn`, `error`) and the details always hold `verbosity` (`minimal`, `normal`, `verbose`), `actor` (`user`, `app`) and `text` (the sentence the activity line shows), plus the facts as their own keys (`runId`, `sourceRoot`, `nodeId`, `counts`, or a Runner event nested whole under `runnerEvent`). Comment lines start with `#`; dropping them loses no fact. The keys are registered in the reference schema, sections 12 and 15. Each backend start writes a `minimal` `viewer_started` entry, which marks where a session begins, after a `# [session]` comment for people. The Viewer's event names differ from the Runner's (`run_result`, not `run_finished`), so the two programs' events are never confused.
  - **Only one backend uses it**: no locking and no sharing between backends are needed, and the file may be deleted and recreated at any time without breaking anything. **[Suggested]** the backend opens the file, appends one entry and closes it again for every entry, so a file deleted while it runs is simply created again by the next entry.
- **UI-72** · **[Decided]** **The activity line has a function to clear the log**. **[Suggested]** a **Clear** button next to the level toggles, asking first ("Clear the activity log? This can't be undone."). Clearing deletes `data/viewer/activity.log` and empties the entries the backend holds for the session, so the activity line is empty too; the next entry, "you cleared the log" (`normal`), starts the file again. It touches nothing else: not the Runner's or the tools' logs, not the cached graphs (`VIEW-09`).
- **UI-73** · **[Decided]** **The activity line counts its entries as "shown / logged"**: the entries shown at the levels selected (`UI-63`), over all the entries the session holds (`UI-69`), at the start of the controls: `2 / 5 [Minimal] [Normal] [Verbose] [Clear] [^]`. It follows every new entry, every level toggled and Clear. *(As built: `actCount` in `ui/src/main.ts`, `#actcount` in `ui/static/index.html`. Checked in headless Firefox, `tests/viewer/browse/activity-count.json`.)*
- **UI-80** · Not in force: there is no static preview; the page itself is checked in headless Firefox (`tests/viewer/browse/`) and reviewed by a person (`BE-95`). Its text: `mvp1/docs_2026-11-10/50_viewer_ui.md`.
- **UI-81** · Not in force, with `UI-80`: `app/viewer/ui/preview.html` was removed. Its text: `mvp1/docs_2026-11-10/50_viewer_ui.md`.

## VIEW

Viewer, from `05_viewer.md`.

- **VIEW-01** · A local HTTP server, reachable only from this machine (bound to `127.0.0.1`).
- **VIEW-02** · Endpoints: specified in `55_viewer_backend.md`, section 8.
- **VIEW-03** · The backend gets everything through the Runner's cache (`--read-cache`), the tool list included; it doesn't read the database (`RUN-27`). It writes only to its own store (`VIEW-06`).
- **VIEW-04** · The backend builds the graph model; the page only displays it (`viewer.md`, section 3.1).
- **VIEW-05** · One run at a time: a second run request while one is running is refused. The Runner's lock (`RUN-30`) enforces this whoever starts the run; the Viewer shows its diagnostic.
- **VIEW-06** · **The Viewer has its own store: `data/viewer/`, JSON files, written only by the Viewer backend.** It is a minimal form of the [Decided] Viewer cache (`viewer.md`, sections 2 and 5), and a starting point: the form may change with what building the Viewer shows (`FND-61`). Nothing else reads it. It never goes into the Runner's database (`ARCH-10`, `ARCH-11`).
  - **`data/viewer/sources/<source-key>/last-good-graph.json`**, one entry per examined source (`VIEW-08`): the graph model of the last successful real run, with that run's `runId` and `finished` time. The backend writes it, atomically, whenever it builds the graph from a cache whose `run.outcome` is `succeeded` and whose `runId` differs from the stored one.
  - **What the page shows** (a run must also pass the Viewer's checks, `VIEW-15`, to be stored, `VIEW-16`): the cache's graph when its run succeeded; otherwise the stored last good graph, marked as not the latest, with the reason (the last run failed, or only a dry run since); with neither, "no real run yet", plus any dry-run diagnostics from the cache. A dry run never changes what is shown (`VIEW-31`).
  - **It can be deleted at any time** (`ARCH-09`): the next successful run rebuilds it. Until then, after a failed run, the page has no good graph to show and says so.
  - **Not in it yet:** node positions (`VIEW-22`), preferences, a pending version (`viewer.md`, section 5). If they are added, the store may move to its own SQLite file in the same folder, never the Runner's.
- **VIEW-07** · **Starting and stopping, for the MVP.** The backend is started by hand from a shell, `zaansouvi-view [--port <n>]`, from any working folder (it finds everything from its own location). It prints the URL to open, with its token, on standard output; it doesn't open the browser itself. It stays running until stopped by hand (Ctrl + C, or ending the process); no Stop button, no idle stop. Starting from the file manager or a desktop shortcut, and opening the browser automatically, stay wishes for later (`FND-62`). A port already in use is a start-up error with a message naming the port and `--port`.
- **VIEW-08** · **Switching the examined source without a restart** (`viewer.md`, section 3.4).
  - The page lists the sources the Viewer has cached and lets the user enter a new source root. Picking one shows its cached graph at once, marked with the time of the run it came from; **Run** runs the Runner on that source root (passed as an argument, `ARCH-03`).
  - **One cache entry per source**, keyed by the source root's absolute real path: `data/viewer/sources/<source-key>/last-good-graph.json` (`<source-key>` a short hash of that path), listed in `data/viewer/sources.json` with the source root and the run it came from. Kept for any number of switches; nothing is dropped automatically.
  - **The Runner's cache holds only the last run's source.** The backend uses it only when its `run.sourceRoot` is the source shown; otherwise it shows the Viewer's entry for that source. `/api/source` reads only files of the source shown, from that entry's file list, under its source root.
  - **An entry the Viewer can't use fails cleanly**: each entry records the graph model's `formatVersion` and the Viewer's version; an entry with another format version, or one that can't be read, isn't shown. The page says why and offers a run for that source, which replaces the entry.
  - **The Runner in the MVP keeps one data folder for every source** (no separate stores per codebase, `toolset.md`, section 5.4, is post-MVP). Switching sources makes `ts-program`, the only tool in the run list (`RUN-33`), run again over the new source's files, since its fingerprint covers every listed file (`TSP-D11`); outputs of the other source's files stay in the stores but are ignored (`RUN-18`). That costs a full run on every switch followed by a run, which is acceptable for the MVP; the Viewer's entries make switching back free until the next run.
- **VIEW-09** · **Clearing the Runner's and the tools' data by hand**: deleting, or moving aside, `data/zaansouvi.sqlite`, `data/runner/` and `data/tools/` while no run holds the lock. `data/viewer/` is left alone, so every source's cached graph survives. The backend copes with the Runner's data missing at any moment: no Runner cache means it shows the Viewer's entries only. Clearing the Viewer's own cache is a separate act: deleting `data/viewer/`, or one source's folder in it.
- **VIEW-10** · Nodes come from every output whose `represents` is `nodes`, plus the files from the file list. Each node's parent is its `parent` field.
- **VIEW-11** · An output whose `represents` is `containment` re-parents the nodes it names: with M3, each symbol's parent becomes its scope instead of its file.
- **VIEW-12** · Edges come from every output whose `represents` is `relations`. A reference becomes an edge from its `from` (the enclosing function, or the file) to the symbol it refers to, started from the scope that node owns (`VIEW-13`); a link becomes an edge from the import symbol to the declaration. A relation whose `to` is `null` is unresolved: it isn't drawn, and the Viewer shows how many there are, with their reasons (`VW-4`, `DATA-10`).
- **VIEW-13** · **Edges are lifted to the nearest visible container, at every level** (`MVP-4`; generalizes the [Decided] file-edge aggregation in `MVP_scope.md`, section 5.1): an edge whose ends are hidden inside a container is drawn between the nearest visible containers, once, with a count, and selecting it lists the edges it stands for, each with its file:line; an edge that starts at a node owning a scope (a scope's `owner`) starts from that scope. At level 1 this joins files, once, with a count; at level 2 it shows each scope with the symbols it is used with. For the test source: the scope `run` has edges to the imports `add` and `PRECISION` in its file, to `counter.add` and `math.PRECISION` through M2's use links, and one unresolved name (`console`). No tool produces file or scope edges.
  *To update for MVP 2:* the example is MVP 1's test source (`test-source/`) with M2 and M3; no example of these rules on `test-source-mvp2/` is documented, since its views at each level are not written down (`expected-mvp2/README.md`; `50_viewer_ui.md`, section 4.1). Which views of `test-source-mvp2` to document is for the user to decide.
- **VIEW-14** · The code that does this reads only `represents`, `containedIn`, `parent`, `owner` (through its `fields` role) and IDs. It has no branch on a tool's name. If it needs one, that is a finding against P4. It doesn't match keys to data itself: it gets the records already grouped by data name from the Runner (`DATA-18`, `RUN-25`), and relies on the agreed key names (`DATA-19`).
- **VIEW-15** · **The Viewer checks every run's output before using or storing it** (`viewer.md`, section 6). The checks are generic, from the field roles only, like `VIEW-14`, run on the server while the graph model is built (`VIEW-04`):
  - **Invalid** (the record is skipped, listed and counted): a node whose `parent` isn't a known node or file; two records with the same ID; a containment record whose child or container isn't known; a relation whose `from` isn't a known node, or whose `to` is neither a known node nor `null`; a scope whose `owner` isn't a known node; a record lacking a field its role needs, or with a malformed Location.
  - **Extra** (listed, not an error): a data name whose `represents` the Viewer doesn't know (not shown); node or edge kinds with no specific style (drawn with a generic one). A record's keys beyond the roles in `fields` are **shown in Details**, every one, as "key: value", so the Viewer uses them and they are not extra data, as `viewer.md`, section 6, defines it: data received but not used. A value it can't show as text (an object or list) is shown as compact JSON.
  - **A graph that can't be built at all** (the Runner's cache unreadable, or the build failing for any reason) is caught for that source alone; the server keeps running (`VIEW-16`).
- **VIEW-16** · **What is shown and stored after the checks.** Per examined source:
  - **Nothing invalid:** the graph is shown and stored as that source's last good graph (`VIEW-08`). Extra data doesn't prevent storing; it is listed in the panel.
  - **Some records invalid:** the new run's graph is shown without them, marked "partly invalid", with the list of skipped records (data name, tool, record ID, problem) and of extra data. It is **not stored**: the source's last good graph stays, and the page can switch to it, marked with its run time. A view never mixes the two runs (`viewer.md`, section 6). Accepting a partly invalid run as the new good one is the pending version of `viewer.md`, section 5: out of the MVP.
  - **Nothing could be built:** the last good graph is shown, marked as not the latest, with the reason; with none, the page says "no good data for this source" and gives the reason.
  - **After a restart or reload,** the same Runner cache is checked again with the same result; nothing about a bad run is remembered except what is in the Runner's cache.
  - **Each entry in `data/viewer/` records its own source root**, so a damaged or missing `sources.json` is rebuilt by reading the entries.
  - **Data that passes the checks but is wrong** can't be caught generically; it is fixed by a new run after the tool is fixed, or by clearing that source's entry by hand (`VIEW-09`).
- **VIEW-17** · **The backend keeps an activity log for the session, every entry tagged `minimal`, `normal` or `verbose`** (MVP only, for debugging and tracking). It logs its own actions and results and the user's actions it receives, including the page's navigation and selections, which the page reports to it. It sends the page the whole session when the page loads and each new entry as it happens. It appends every entry to a single file, `data/viewer/activity.log`, created if missing; only one backend uses it, so it may be deleted and recreated at any time without breaking anything; the activity line can clear it (`UI-71`, `UI-72`). The page shows them in the activity line, with a toggle per level (`50_viewer_ui.md`, `UI-62` to `UI-69`). Which entry gets which level is suggested in `UI-62`.
- **VIEW-18** · **Accepted for the backend**: run events and activity entries reach the page by server-sent events; the security minimum of `55_viewer_backend.md`, section 9: a token set as a session cookie, `Host` and `Origin` checks, reads limited to the source's listed files and to `data/`, nothing loaded from the internet; the graph rules of `50_viewer_ui.md`, `UI-34` and `UI-36`, and the visual key of `UI-41`; the page's TypeScript compiled with `tsc`, no bundler, Cytoscape served from the local install. The backend in full: `55_viewer_backend.md`.
- **VIEW-20** · Double-click a node to go one level down into it; a breadcrumb at the top goes back up. The mouse wheel only zooms the current level (`viewer.md`, section 4.9; Ctrl + wheel is out of the MVP).
- **VIEW-21** · Not in force in MVP 2: the levels follow TypeScript's nesting, at any depth (`TSP-D8`, `VIEW-50`). MVP 1 text: `mvp1/docs_2026-11-10/05_viewer.md`.
- **VIEW-22** · Layout: an automatic layout per level; nodes can be dragged. Positions are not saved in the MVP.
- **VIEW-23** · Visual language, kept minimal: one shape per node kind (file, scope, function, variable, parameter, import; and the kinds `ts-program` gives: class, interface, type alias, enum, enum member, namespace, method, constructor, accessor, property; and the listed folders, links and other entries, `UI-48`); declarations solid, references dashed; links in a separate color. The shapes are in `50_viewer_ui.md`, `UI-41`.
- **VIEW-30** · Selecting a node or edge shows, in a side panel: its kind, name, file:line, and the source line with the lines around it (from `/api/source`).
- **VIEW-31** · A tool panel lists the tools of the Runner's cache in the stored order (`ts-program` alone, `RUN-33`), read-only, each marked as enabled (all are, in the MVP), with its latest result and a link to its log. After a dry-run-only pass, it also shows each invocation's go / no-go and error from the dry-run part of the Runner's cache (`RUN-27`); the graph doesn't change. Each tool's diagnostics are listed there too, never in the graph: from each invocation's result in the cache after a real run, and from the dry-run part after a dry-run-only pass (`DATA-14`, `RUN-27`).
- **VIEW-32** · Two buttons: **Run** and **Dry run**. While running, the panel shows each `tool_skipped`, `tool_dry_run` and `tool_run` event as it arrives (a skipped tool in grey, marked up to date), with go / no-go and errors. A no-go or failure is shown in red, with the message and the location if there is one.
- **VIEW-33** · After a run or a dry run started from the page finishes, the backend announces `graph_updated` on the event stream; for a real run of the source shown, the page reloads the graph from `GET /api/graph` (`BE-57`), and for either it reloads the Tools pane from `GET /api/tools` (`graph_updated` in `app/viewer/server/src/server.ts` and `ui/src/main.ts`). Nothing refreshes on its own otherwise. The Viewer never starts a run on its own: the run button (`/api/run`) is the user's way to reload the graph, and is a manual run that replaces the Runner's cache, like a command-line run (`RUN-27`).
- **VIEW-40** · Every name, path and source line is shown as text, never as HTML (`security.md`, section 8).
- **VIEW-50** · **[Decided]** As in the MVP 2 schema, section 10: every listed entry is a node at the top level, with its status and, for a file, its type (`UI-47`, `UI-48`); a node's container may be another symbol, so levels go to any depth; built-ins are listed under each view's `builtins`, apart from `unresolved`; a record's other keys are kept as `attrs` and shown in Details (`VIEW-15`); source lines are served only for files a tool read as text (`security.md`, section 7). A stored graph of format 1 is unusable and rebuilt by the next run.
